note: The article's nine forms, in the article's order. Each score is a judgment of a form, not a measurement of a tree. A higher total is not a rank of the implementations on this page. n/a: the article does not score a form it reads as unable to apply to Bitcoin.

rows.name: Direct democracy
rows.na_reason: Not scored: the article reads this form as unable to apply to Bitcoin
rows.reading: Cannot apply. Participants are pseudonymous, and identities are free to create, so votes cannot be counted.

rows.name: Token-weighted voting
rows.na_reason: Not scored: the article reads this form as unable to apply to Bitcoin
rows.reading: Cannot apply. Bitcoin has no governance token.

rows.name: Single maintainer
rows.reading: Can apply, at a legitimacy cost. One obvious author and no written rule.

rows.name: Foundation steward
rows.reading: Can apply, with legal exposure. A legal entity is one place a suit or a rule can land.

rows.name: Informal oligarchy
rows.reading: The current repository form in the article. A few people merge, chosen by pull request and a meeting, with no written rule for keys or review.

rows.name: Formal oligarchy
rows.reading: The same small set, with published rules for selection, review, and removal.

rows.name: Elected council
rows.reading: Can apply, with limits. Bitcoin has no agreed electorate.

rows.name: Mixed constitution
rows.reading: Separate powers and written thresholds. Untested at Bitcoin's scale. The BLVM layer table is a written version of this shape. This page does not score that projection.

rows.name: Ostrom commons
rows.reading: Bounded membership, monitoring, and a cheap way to dispute. The cases behind the principles were small and local.
